description:
Raised by the implementing agent 2026-08-11 as part of op-jyyp.1 (landed in commit 4feb6c84, crates/tuas_boussinesq_solver/.../solid_database/nuclear_graphite.rs, 871 lines, 6 V&V tests). Both assumptions are documented at the site rather than hidden, but both should be reviewed before any result depending on them is trusted.

1. ONE cp CURVE SERVES BOTH GRADES. The specific-heat table is grade-insensitive: NuclearGraphiteMatrixA3 and NuclearGraphiteIG110 dispatch to the same shared enthalpy and cp functions. The enum arms were deliberately duplicated per variant rather than collapsed into an or-pattern, precisely so this decision stays greppable and has to be revisited explicitly if the assumption is challenged. Check whether the grades genuinely share a cp curve within the accuracy this work needs.

2. THE A3 DAMAGE FACTOR IS APPLIED TO IG-110, WHICH THE VTB DOES NOT DO. The fast-neutron-fluence conductivity degradation was fitted for matrix graphite A3 and is being reused for IG-110. The source the correlations came from does not make that extension. Irradiated reflector conductivity drives the passive decay-heat path, so if IG-110 degrades differently this propagates straight into the loss-of-forced-cooling result — the exact place where an optimistic error makes the safety case look better than it is.

WHAT THE TESTS ACTUALLY ESTABLISH, per the implementing agent: "Nothing here is checked against HTR-10 measurements. The tests verify transcription and interpolation against hand evaluations of the same formulas — that is all they establish." The word "validated" appears nowhere in the added code or docs, correctly.

Measured behaviour for reference: damage factor is 1.0 at zero fluence and 0.139 at gam = 15, still positive, with the zero crossing near gam = 19. The fluence gate is [0, 15] and returns an error rather than clamping.
title: TUAS nuclear graphite: two documented assumptions carrying real physical risk

description: A reusable eframe::App-adjacent scaffold (physics-thread spawning + Arc<Mutex<_>> clone-on-read pattern, panel/page dispatch) that tampines/examples/fhr_sim_v2 and htgr_sim_v1 can build on, instead of each simulator re-deriving the same threading boilerplate fresh. Real, working code -- the threading/locking pattern is simple and already proven twice in existing examples; the content of any given panel is still the calling application's job.
title: digital-twin-gui: app_scaffold/ -- reusable eframe::App threading/locking scaffold (real code)
